chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Pray them both after dawn rises. The proper way of understanding these reports is one of two possibilities. One of them is that this is a concession for one who prays the two rakʿahs at the beginning of dawn as a precaution, so that the time of the obligatory prayer may become clear with certainty. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.اسْتِظْهَارًا: as a precautionary measure or for greater certainty
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn; the time related to the beginning of the fajr prayer period
key_terms.الْيَقِينِ: certainty; clear assurance regarding the entry of prayer time
key_terms.رُخْصَةً: a concession or allowance granted in a matter of practice
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the time of the obligatory prayer
key_terms.يُصَلِّيهِمَا: he prays the two units; referring to the two rakʿahs of fajr

ai.seo_question: When should the two rakʿahs of fajr be prayed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the time of the two rakʿahs of fajr and indicates that praying them after the rise of dawn is the basis. It also explains that reports allowing them at the very beginning of dawn may be understood as a concession taken for precaution until the time of the obligatory prayer is known with certainty.
